construction_and_coverage.construction: Symmetric spectral construction and dual weights described in the source-linked Proof map; block distance scale D gives joint start distance sqrt(2)D.
construction_and_coverage.coverage: All deterministic sequences and outputs satisfying Eq.(11); the argument controls reachable spans rather than proving an information-theoretic impossibility for arbitrary query locations.
escape_limits: Arbitrary out-of-span query points or unrestricted reported output are outside Theorem 3.
Direct access to and solution of the full matrix system is not a covered escape-proof model; methods must still obey the stated class.
construction_and_coverage.oracle_realization: For L=<Ax-b,y-c> with symmetric A, exact feedback is (A(y-c),Ax-b); no noise, sampling or stochastic reuse model is assumed.

content.intended_use: A lower bound under separate linear-span restrictions, with biaffine sharpness

proofs.locator: Main Eq.(13)-(23), Lemmas 3-4; supplement C.1-C.4 Eq.(51)-(64)
map: Main pp.5-6 choose symmetric A with ||A||<=R and b in range(A) from Lemma 3; let c=x_min, the minimum-norm solution of Ax=b. Set L(x,y)=<Ax-b,y-c>. Exact gradients are A(y-c) and Ax-b, so G=(A(y-c),b-Ax). The closest zero-start saddle is (x_min,x_min).

C.1 p.9 gives translation b0=b-Ax^0, c0=c-y^0 and block subspace recurrences X_(j+1)=span{A^T c0}+A^T Y_j, Y_(j+1)=span{b0}+A X_j. For the symmetric construction Ac=b, both block iterates belong to span{b,Ab,...,A^(k-1)b}.

C.2-C.3 pp.10-12 reduce x=q(A)b to residual p(A)b with p(t)=1-tq(t). With m=floor(k/2), the Chebyshev polynomial p*_k(t)=(-1)^m R T_(2m+1)(t/R)/((2m+1)t), extended polynomially at zero, has minimax value R/(2m+1), Eq.(58). Symmetrization and equioscillation give the source optimality argument.

C.3 p.12 uses dual weights mu_j>=0 summing to one at lambda_j=R cos((2m+1-j)pi/(2m+1)). Define A e_j=lambda_j e_j and A=0 off their span, x_min=D sum_j sqrt(mu_j)e_j, b=A x_min. Strong duality of Eq.(61)-(62) gives one spectral instance hard for every polynomial of degree <=k-1. n>=k+2 accommodates these directions.

Main p.6 adds the two block residual bounds to obtain Eq.(12). Main pp.6-7 Eq.(17)-(23) and supplement C.4 p.13 relate biaffine saddle operators to skew-symmetric linear equations; the polynomial upper witness from Lemma 4 gives the sharpness chain.

assumptions: Exact gradient feedback at successive query points; all intermediate query points must be included in the index.
Both query sequence and output z^k satisfy the separate block spans; the initial point is fixed.
The hard instance is R-smooth biaffine and has a saddle point.
statement.conclusion: ||grad L(z^k)||^2 >= R^2 ||z^0-z*||^2/(2 floor(k/2)+1)^2. Theorem 3 also states this bound cannot be improved using biaffine functions: Section 3.2 Eq.(16)-(21) gives C(A_sep;biaffine_R,D,k)=R^2 D^2/(2 floor(k/2)+1)^2, and equality for A_sim follows in that chain. Sharpness here is over biaffine instances, not over every smooth convex-concave function.
statement.objects_and_definitions: A_sep is the deterministic class satisfying, for every j>=1, x^j in x^0+span{grad_x L(z^i):0<=i<j} and y^j in y^0+span{grad_y L(z^i):0<=i<j}; z^j=(x^j,y^j), Eq.(11). L is biaffine on R^n x R^n. R-smooth means G=(grad_x L,-grad_y L) is R-Lipschitz. z* is the saddle point closest to z^0. For sharpness, C(A;F,D,k) is the worst squared-gradient residual after k indexed steps over F and starts within distance D of a saddle point; C(class;F,D,k)=inf over methods in the class of this worst case (Section 3.2). A_sim is the subclass with z^j in z^0+span{G(z^i):0<=i<j}, Eq.(10).
statement.parameter_domains: R>0; k integer >=0; n integer >=k+2. Sharpness uses distance bound D>0.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every R>0, integer k>=0 and n>=k+2, and any fixed initial point z^0, there exists an R-smooth biaffine L such that every deterministic method in A_sep satisfies the bound at k. Translation of the zero-start construction is addressed in C.1. No unrestricted or randomized-Oracle conclusion is included.
